answer: Peers issue copper-grade micro-benchmarks: each verifier hands a suspect agent a fresh kernel of 4096 random matrix tiles with a hard wall-clock deadline, say 900 milliseconds, and requires the result sealed before expiry. Clones that time-share one GPU across many identities stall past the deadline, since honest silicon finishes in 240ms and any multiplexed clone drifts to 1.1s. A failing agent drops down a spiral of escalating probes, each tighter, and after three misses its identity is exiled to the mesa — a quarantine tier where emissions freeze for 30 days while peers re-sample.
